title: Performance, concurrency and resilience hardening

environment.profile: local controlled acceptance on Darwin arm64; synthetic data only

BIO-OPS-007-AC01.finding: Two distinct replacement activations are serialized and only the latest live sequence can activate; exactly one attempt succeeds and one card remains active.

BIO-OPS-007-AC02.finding: Overlapping reconnect passes preserve single-flight and atomic claims, upload each mutation once, and coalesce a recovery pass after an in-flight network failure.

BIO-OPS-007-AC03.finding: Thirty-one post-warmup loopback HTTP samples were retained for a live API endpoint and production-built approved UI page, with raw values and median/p95/p99 statistics.

BIO-OPS-007-AC04.finding: Executable database-create, queue-append and mid-request network interruptions prove recovery, integrity, retry, no loss and no duplicate effects.

BIO-OPS-007-AC05.finding: Bounded local workload, parallelism, memory-headroom, duration and recovery recommendations are documented for 16, 32 and 64 GB laptops.

commands.result: PASS unrestricted (15/15); local Flutter SDK cache is sandbox read-only

disclosures: Latency figures are single-client loopback baselines for comparison on one laptop, not production service-level objectives or capacity claims.
The accepted production fix is also present on the owning feature/BIO-CRD-006 branch; integration into develop remains the orchestrator's responsibility.

final_acceptance.reason: AC01-AC05 map to executable tests and retained evidence. The replacement-card race is fixed and discriminated, database/queue/network interruptions exercise the correct boundaries, and latency data measures real local HTTP requests rather than build or runner time.
